fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a True and False Quiz
fields.features_subheading: Describe the statements, the pass mark, and who sees the scores. Emergent builds the quiz and the table that holds every answer.
fields.feature_1:
Statements drafted from your notes

Paste a unit outline or a policy page, and Emergent drafts true and false statements from it, about half of them false. A follow-up prompt rewords a statement that gives itself away.
fields.feature_2:
A rewrite box on every false answer

When a taker marks a statement false, the app can ask for a corrected version. You read the rewrites in one list and accept or return each. A lucky tap on False earns no point.
fields.feature_3:
Sure or Guessing beside each answer

Takers mark each of their answers Sure or Guessing. The table lists the wrong answers marked Sure apart from wrong guesses. Reteach what a class believed, not what it guessed.
fields.feature_4:
Every answer saved as a row

Each answer is saved with the taker, the statement, and the confidence mark, in a database you own. Sort by statement to see which one the most takers got wrong, and by whom.
fields.feature_5:
A pass mark that sends an email

Set a pass mark such as 11 of 12, and the app emails a manager or teacher each time a taker lands below it. Emergent puts no cap on responses, for one class or a whole district.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and the full code

Host the quiz on your own domain; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and reuse it next term.

fields.usecase_heading: Where a True and False Quiz Does Real Work
fields.tab_content_1:
A false answer counts only after the rewrite is accepted

Renata Pasternak's 29 seventh-grade geography students at Halloran Ridge Middle School answer 20 statements, 10 of them false. Marking one false opens a box to rewrite it so it is true, and the point counts once she accepts the rewrite. On Friday, 112 rewrites came in. She accepted 87 and sent 25 back.
fields.tab_content_2:
Each hire under 11 of 12 sets off an email

New hires at Gilsland Cycle Co.'s 3 shops answer 12 true or false statements on the returns policy. The pass mark is 11 of 12. A lower score emails service manager Chidi Nkemdirim the statements that hire missed. This spring, 9 of 13 hires passed on the first try, and the other 4 retook it after a walk-through.
fields.tab_content_3:
Bitter Enders won it, 14 of 15 right

Thursday trivia at Calder Flats Taproom ends with a 15-statement true or false round, answered on phones one statement at a time. Last Thursday, 22 teams played. The leaderboard updates after each statement, and the host reads it from a tablet behind the bar. Bitter Enders won with 14 of 15, and no team got all 15.
fields.tab_content_4:
Sure but wrong: 19 students on one statement

Hanne Ruckert asks the 58 students in her earth science course at Osterbrook Community College to mark each of 16 answers Sure or Guessing. On the statement that Earth's air is mostly oxygen, 19 answered True and marked it Sure, more than on any other. That statement now opens Tuesday's lecture.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a True and False Quiz Template
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a true and false quiz template with fair statements, a clear pass mark, and scores you can act on.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what one score should tell you
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask for a fix on false answers
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the job the quiz does before you write a statement: a pass mark on a policy, a review before a unit test, or a trivia round. Put that job and the people taking it in your prompt, and Emergent drafts statements in their words.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Start from facts the takers should know, then make about half of them false by changing one detail, such as a name, a number, or a place. A statement that is false in only one spot tests the fact, not how fast someone reads.
fields.howto_step_3_des: A statement that joins two claims is false if either half is wrong, and takers cannot tell which half you meant. Split it in two. Cut words like always and never too, since they hint at the answer before the taker thinks.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add a rewrite box to every statement a taker calls false, and count the point only once the fix is right. Someone guessing at random on 20 statements lands near 10, and the rewrites show who knew the answer.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set the pass mark and who hears
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick the pass mark from what a miss costs: 11 of 12 for a policy new hires use on day one, a lower bar for a practice round. Then name the person who gets an email when a score falls under it.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Have 3 people take the quiz on their phones before anyone else does. If all 3 miss the same statement, reread its wording first. Then check that each answer reached the results table under the right name.
fields.howto_step_7_des: After the first round, sort the results by statement and look at the 3 with the most wrong answers. Reword the ones that misled careful takers, and reteach the ones that exposed a real gap.

faq_plan.q: What is a true and false quiz template?
faq_plan.a: A true and false quiz template is a reusable quiz layout where each item is a statement the taker marks True or False. It holds the statements, the right answer to each, and the scoring rules. Swap in new statements for the next unit or team, and the rest stays as it was.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a true and false quiz template?
faq_plan.a: Write the statements, about half of them false, and mark the right answer to each. Then decide the pass mark and who reads the results. With Emergent's AI survey builder, you describe that quiz in one prompt and get a working app that scores every answer and keeps it in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What should a true false quiz maker do beyond adding up the score?
faq_plan.a: It should show which statements people missed, not only each person's total. Look for a true false quiz maker that saves every answer by statement, lets takers correct a statement they mark false, and emails someone when a score falls under the pass mark. Emergent builds all three from a prompt, with no cap on responses.

faq_plan.q: How many statements should a true or false quiz have?
faq_plan.a: Use at least 10 for any quiz that counts. With only 2 options, a pure guesser averages half right, and on a 4-statement quiz that guesser scores 4 of 4 one time in 16.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep students from guessing on a true or false quiz?
faq_plan.a: Give every guess a cost. Ask students to rewrite each statement they mark false, or to mark every answer Sure or Guessing, and score the rewrite or the confidence along with the answer. Either way, a coin-flip answer stops earning full credit.

faq_plan.q: Should a true or false quiz have equal numbers of true and false statements?
faq_plan.a: Close to equal, but not exactly. If takers learn that half of every quiz is false, they can count their answers and adjust the last few. On a 20-statement quiz, write 8 to 12 of them as false, and change the split from one quiz to the next.

faq_plan.q: How do I write a false statement for a true or false quiz without tricking people?
faq_plan.a: Change one detail in a true statement the takers should know, such as a date, a number, or a name, and keep the rest as it was taught. Skip double negatives, and never hide the error in a small word like not. The statement should be false because of the fact it tests.

faq_plan.q: Can a true or false quiz maker grade a corrected answer?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the quiz is built for it. With Emergent, you can build a quiz app that checks a rewrite against a list of accepted wordings, or holds the point until a teacher reads it. A list suits short fixes like a place name, and a teacher's read suits a full sentence.

faq_plan.q: Can I reuse a true and false quiz template for a new topic each week?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Keep the layout, the scoring, and the pass mark, and replace only the statements. In Emergent, a follow-up prompt swaps in next week's statements, and every week's answers land in the same results table, tagged by week for a side-by-side view.

faq_plan.q: Can I run a true or false quiz as a live game for a group?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Players answer on their phones, one statement per screen, while a leaderboard on a shared screen updates after each one. Keep every statement short enough to read in a few seconds, and hold back one tiebreaker question with a number answer for teams that finish level.

quiz.title: True or False Quiz: 8 Statements on Earth, Space, and History
quiz.intro: Eight statements, four of them false. Mark each one True or False; your score and a source for every answer show at the end.

questions.text: True or false: The Atlantic is the largest ocean on Earth.
questions.explanation: False. The Pacific is the largest ocean basin, and the deepest too.

source.quote: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of the world ocean basins

questions.text: True or false: Lake Superior is the largest body of fresh water in the world by surface area.
questions.explanation: True. Measured by surface area, no lake on Earth holds more fresh water across its top.

source.quote: Lake Superior is the largest body of fresh water in the world by surface area

questions.text: True or false: Mercury is the hottest planet because it sits closest to the Sun.
questions.explanation: False. Venus is hotter, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.

source.quote: Venus is the hottest planet in our solar system

questions.text: True or false: Mars has two small moons.
questions.explanation: True. Their names are Phobos and Deimos.

source.quote: Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos

questions.text: True or false: The blue whale is the largest animal on Earth.
questions.explanation: True. No animal alive today, on land or at sea, is larger.

source.quote: The blue whale is the largest animal on Earth

questions.text: True or false: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from the people of Britain.
questions.explanation: False. It was a gift of friendship from the people of France to the United States.

source.quote: A gift of friendship from the people of France to the United States

questions.text: True or false: Earth's atmosphere is mostly oxygen.
questions.explanation: False. Nitrogen makes up 78% of the air and oxygen 21%.

source.quote: Earth's atmosphere is 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen and 1% other ingredients

questions.text: True or false: Yellowstone became a national park in 1872.
questions.explanation: True. President Ulysses S. Grant signed the act that created it on March 1, 1872.

source.quote: On March 1, 1872, President Ulysses S. Grant signed the Yellowstone National Park Protection Act into law
